prospect.name: Jake Brenner
prospect.location: Sacramento, California, USA (works in Oakland, California)
prospect.occupation: Firefighter, Oakland Fire Department — two days on, four days off
prospect.training_background: Lifelong athlete; played rugby through college; weighed 240 lb in college then lost 60 lb on pure calisthenics during COVID; heavy barbell training in his firefighter-academy period which he says wrecked his joints; department introduced him to kettlebells and functional work; has followed Trevor on Instagram for about six weeks and been doing his workouts two to three days a week for roughly a month
prospect.medical: Prescribed Adderall and self-reports taking "a ton of Adderall at work" plus roughly 400 mg caffeine per day. Reports repeated near-collapse at fires — "at the end of every fire I literally feel like I'm gonna die... I couldn't feel my feet" — and a persistent cognitive fog on days without stimulants. Historic joint pain in knees and elbows from barbell training, self-reported as resolved. Chronically tight hips, not painful. Describes a mentally draining year of occupational trauma exposure, a negative inner voice, and being "in this slump". No clinician was mentioned and none was asked about.

signals: Explicitly lost ground and knows it: "I've been a very fit person my entire life... then once I actually started working, I hit this like mental wall... my overall discipline in the gym has gone like complete nowhere"
Wants a former self back and names the exact number: "My fastest and most athletic, I feel like, at 180 to 185"
Carries visible regret — "I forget about these things that I used to do and what was effective for me... I have been in great shape, like crazy good shape"
Hard season is occupational rather than medical (trauma exposure on the job), but the shape of it is rebuilder rather than prehab-fighter — no active diagnosis or treatment is being fought

goals.text: Stop burning out and feeling sluggish on the fire ground so he is safe and effective at work
Lose 10-20 lb of body fat and get back to a muscular, strong 185-190
Get back to the inner voice that pushes rather than drags — regain mental resilience and confidence
Stop relying on Adderall and 400 mg of caffeine a day to function
Learn active stretching and mobility properly so his hips open up
Be able to say honestly that he gave his best for the people he serves
Establish a lifestyle now that lasts the next 31 years of his career and into fatherhood
Build "a machine, rather than just muscles" — training that transfers directly to the job

pains.text: Burns out to the point of near-collapse at every fire — "the last fire I was on, I was walking around and I couldn't feel my feet"
Dependent on prescribed Adderall and two Celsius energy drinks daily to stay focused and alert
Occupational trauma exposure — "super mentally draining of like seeing all this tragedy around you and taking it home"
Inner voice turned negative; "disappointed, so I'm just giving up all the time because I'm just used to being disappointed in myself"
Two steps forward two steps back for at least a year — hits it for a month then something happens and it collapses
Cooks from scratch at the firehouse but has no energy to cook at home, so defaults to DoorDash and Chipotle
Workouts at the firehouse get constantly interrupted because Oakland runs busy at all hours
Chronically tight hips and no knowledge of how to stretch or open the body up
Doesn't know which of the things that worked for him before to trust — "what type of workouts am I doing? What's going to work?"
Carries the what-ifs from calls that went badly — "do I now have to talk to someone's wife about how their husband died in there... was I trying my best?"

evidence: Immediate yes on the number with no objection of any kind: rep — "we have an investment of 6k"; Jake — "Okay, yeah... Let's get started?" / "Yeah."
Payment capture began live on the call — rep asked "do you have like a credit card?", then took name on card ("Jacob Brenner"), email, country and started the billing address
Commitment was locked before the presentation, not after: "I'm ready to go, pretty much. Let's do it." at 00:41:00

Counter-evidence: the recording truncates mid-billing-address at 01:00:24 ("Address? 145. Let me actually just... Can we just... Whiting?"), so no payment confirmation, no signed agreement and no confirmed Trevor onboarding slot are on the record. Card details were taken directly rather than a link being sent, so the client close rule is applied by analogy.
outcome.next_step: Onboarding call with Trevor tomorrow or Thursday — rep said he would check Trevor's calendar and that it might even be same-day. Not confirmed on the recording.

notable.note: Cleanest process call in the batch and it closed at full price in under an hour with zero objections. The concern is entirely clinical, not commercial: a 26-year-old firefighter disclosed repeated exertional near-collapse ("I couldn't feel my feet"), prescribed Adderall taken in self-described large amounts, and 400 mg of caffeine a day, and was sold high-intensity loaded ballistic training with the explicit promise he would not need the medication any more. Nobody asked whether a doctor had been consulted. Sleep was never asked about at all despite a 48-hour-on shift pattern.

quality.notes: Heavy and continuous label inversion — the very first exchange has the rep's own line "I'm calling from Sacramento, California" attributed to him rather than Jake, and long stretches from 00:06:00 to 00:07:00 and 00:20:54 to 00:21:48 run under the wrong label entirely. Role read from content throughout. The file also ends abruptly mid-sentence during payment capture, so the tail of the call is missing.
